topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs together with their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver mutations and the clinical challenges posed by bypass resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are engineered to recognize surface antigens and deliver targeted cytotoxicity.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of immune surveillance in oncology and the therapeutic mechanisms of checkpoint blockade, bispecific engagers, and engineered CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate long-term trends in cancer mortality, persistent clinical challenges, and future paradigms for managing oncological disease.
